title: Lightly Row
short: Traditional (German folk song “Hänschen  · G 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: A two-chord song in G. The tune uses the open 4th string (G) and the first string (A, B, C and D at frets 0, 2, 3 and 5), so the picking hand jumps across the strings: that’s normal on a ukulele, whose highest and lowest notes sit on the two outside strings. To strum, use down-up eighth notes; in bars 7 and 15 change from G to D7 halfway through the bar.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: German folk song from the first half of the 1800s, sung in English as “Lightly Row”

sources.name: Melody as in our piano version of Lightly Row, which was checked note by note against the “Hänschen klein” page of the German Wikibooks songbook (LilyPond). The chords follow that version’s left hand. Our checking script compares the two melodies beat by beat.
